judge.rationale: The implementation is a textbook example of Pythonic clarity and directness. It uses a set union to enumerate all fields exactly once, iterates with a simple for-loop (flat, no nesting beyond one level), uses dict.get with a None sentinel to naturally handle added/removed fields, builds explicit records with the required keys, and sorts in a single readable lambda. There is no abstraction overhead, no helper classes, no magic, and every line is locally auditable. It satisfies all three SRL-3 requirements: each change is an explicit record with field/before/after, nothing is collapsed into summaries, and the field labels are preserved verbatim.
